title: How to Manage Corporate Short-Stay Operations With Multiple Branches
summary: See how to manage corporate short-stay operations spread across multiple branches and entities.
body_markdown:
Managing corporate short-stay operations across multiple branches means each branch runs the same core process, while head office gets a consolidated view across the entire operation, with pricing scaling by users rather than by branch count. In **Jestor** , this uses the same multi-entity, multi-CNPJ structure built for holdings and franchises generally.


Corporate short-stay operators — those managing properties as part of a larger, structured business — need the consistency of a shared process without losing branch-level operational flexibility.


## What multi-branch corporate operations struggle with


- Each branch building its own local process, diverging in quality and consistency
- No consolidated financial or operational view across the whole corporate structure
- Inconsistent guest experience between branches serving similar markets
- Cost or complexity increasing disproportionately with every new branch


## How multi-branch corporate management works


- One process template applies across every connected branch or entity
- Multiple **Omie** or **Conta Azul** accounts connect under one overall structure
- Approval **alçadas** can be centralized or configured per branch
- Head office gets a consolidated dashboard across the entire corporate structure


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Pricing is based on users, not the number of branches or connected accounts
- One shared template keeps guest experience and operations consistent across branches
- Consolidated dashboards give head office visibility without manual compilation
- The same structure scales from a handful of branches to a large corporate network


Corporate multi-branch gap How a shared structure helps


Each branch builds independently One shared, consistent template


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does adding a new branch increase cost significantly?** No, pricing is based on users, not the number of branches. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can branches keep some local flexibility?** Yes, within a shared overall structure.


**Does head office see consolidated performance across all branches?** Yes, through a consolidated dashboard.
